correctness.rationale: Modulo 3 the three classes follow 0→1→2→2. For both unit classes the derivative is a unit, so simple-root lifting supplies one predecessor in each unit class at each periodic target. This makes the class 2 a permutation and gives the claimed depth strata and unique transient predecessor. For depth-two points the exact identity F²(x)−2=x²(x²−4) gives twice the valuation of x and leading digit 2 until truncation. The zero-difference target counts multiples of 3^ceil(k/2). At any allowed nonzero difference with s=2v, dividing by 3^(2v) gives two simple unit roots modulo 3, lifted to modulus 3^(k−2v) and repeated 3^v times in the original variable, which gives the fibre formula. The multiplier y+2 preserves both shell invariants. On s≥2, y−F(y) has valuation s+1 because v_3(y+1)=1. For an iterate H with displacement valuation m≥3 and derivative 1 mod 3, the integral Taylor expansion gives the displacement of H³ as (1+H′+H′²) times the original modulo 3^(2m); the multiplier has valuation one. An iterate count prime to 3 preserves the displacement valuation by first-order iteration. This proves the period equals the cardinality of its leading-digit sector, including singleton sectors and k=1 with only the special root. The uploaded verifier was inspected, not executed. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/branches/47e5fac2-6e75-447e-b393-f5f363bb1e3c/independent_check.py 4 (also with argument 8); observations are in independent_k4.txt and independent_k8.txt there. Every fibre and rich shell was checked in those finite cases (11 cycles, 2 rich at k=4; 27 cycles, 4 rich at k=8, including the root 2 in each). Those checks are corroboration, not the all-k proof.

value.rationale: The result identifies exactly how transient states are distributed in a natural nonpermutation dynamical system, distinguishing branch-bearing cycles from cycles with the same possible lengths but no such branches. It gives a local tree invariant at every periodic vertex for arbitrarily deep moduli and explains why uniform depth strata do not imply uniform trees. The ternary orbit argument addresses a different local lifting regime from the analogous five-adic calculation.
